title: Elaine V. Schroeder Obituary Oct 15, 2026 - Trimble Funeral Home & Crematory
content:
Jan 3, 1937 — Oct 15, 2026 Davenport, Iowa 1530 E 39th St,
                                
                                
                                                                Davenport,
                                
                                IA 52807 Elaine V. Schroeder, 89, of Davenport, Iowa, passed away Thursday, October 15, 2026, at MercyOne Genesis Davenport Medical Center. Graveside services will be held at 11:00 a.m. Tuesday, October 20, at Pine Hill Cemetery. Trimble Funeral Home & Crematory, Moline, is assisting the family. Memorials may be made to Gilda’s Club. The former Elaine Velma Schlichting was born January 3, 1937, in Davenport, the daughter of Leroy and Florence (Clark) Schlichting. She graduated from Davenport High School in 1956 and married the love of her life, Leo Louis Schroeder, on October 2, 1966. Elaine worked at Arnold’s Clothing and Bayer’s Real Estate, but her greatest joy came from being a homemaker and building a life with Leo. Together, they raised their three children until his untimely passing on May 8, 1981. Though his loss was profound, Elaine continued to devote herself to the family they had created. Family remained at the heart of Elaine’s life, and nothing brought her greater happiness than time spent with her grandchildren, who were her greatest pride and joy. She treasured watching her family grow and the special memories they shared. Elaine had a love for music and played the organ in her younger years. She was a member and past president of the Hammond Organ Society and also belonged to the Orchid Society. She enjoyed caring for plants and crocheting. Elaine is survived by three children, Michelle McKinnis of Davenport, Michael (Dawn) Schroeder of Bettendorf, and Lisa Ackerman of Ames, Iowa; and her grandchildren, Alan-Michael (Daniela) Schroeder, Sean Ackerman, Alec Ackerman, Zach Schroeder, Madison McKinnis, Olivia McKinnis, and Kylie McKinnis. She was preceded in death by her parents; her husband, Leo; her son-in-law, Keith McKinnis; and her sister, Elmira Schlichting. title: This Carbon-Fiber Body Kit Makes the Cadillac Escalade-V Look Like the Loudest SUV in Town - Car and Driver
content: Want everyone to know you bought the supercharged Caddy? Here you go. Cadillac lightly facelifted the Escalade for the 2025 model year, showing particular restraint with the top-flight V variant. Despite packing a supercharged 6.2-liter V-8 with 682 horsepower under the hood, the V basically looks identical to more modestly powered Escalades. It’s perhaps taking a page from the full-size Range Rover playbook, where big power is not something you necessarily advertise. However, there are always going to be customers who bought the most powerful Escalade partially because they wanted everyone to notice. For these individuals, may we present the Larte Design Esthete body kit for the Escalade-V, offering a more visually striking take on the top-of-the-line Caddy SUV. Emphasis on striking, as looking at these pictures feels a bit like getting punched in the face. See all results for new 2026 Cadillac Escalade / Escalade ESV for sale near 85032 Larte Design is not exactly known for pulling its punches, having built over-the-top body kits for everything from the Mercedes-AMG G63 to the BMW X6 M. It takes a special sort of brain to look at a Lamborghini Urus and decide that the factory look simply isn't aggressive enough, and you can find those minds at Larte's Turin design studio. It's a bit like the Scoville scale in the world of hot sauce, where whether more is better isn’t really up for discussion. More is more. That’s the whole point. And, it has to be said, the Larte Design team does put a great deal of effort into the engineering behind its offerings. A few years back, it came up with pink carbon-fiber bodywork for the Escalade, and rather than just coating the elements with a tinted clearcoat, the carbon fiber weave itself was impregnated with the color. Here, the Escalade-V gets a two-tone exterior in gloss black and red, with all of the exterior design elements formed of dry carbon. There’s a massive vented hood, a new front grille, aggressive wheel-arch extensions, carbon-fiber rings over the 24-inch multispoke wheels, and a rear spoiler and diffuser that would make the Batmobile proud. Thinking about that jutting front splitter encountering a parking curb is making us wince. While the Larte Design body kit obviously isn’t for everyone, it’ll attract anyone who wants their supercharged Caddy to look like what Jeff Bezos would drive if he lived in the Mad Max universe. From the factory, there’s something to be said for the Escalade-V’s “speak softly and carry a big stick” approach. This body kit eliminates the speak softly part. title: Storylines | Royals v. Current: A Contest Between Two Top Five Sides - Real Salt Lake
content: Utah Royals FC host fifth-seeded Kansas City Current at America First Field in its first of two home matches. The Royals will hope to take another step forward to extending its lead at the top of the table heading into the final three games of the season. This edition of Storylines will take a look at the Royals’ most reliable defender, and a battle between two teams hoping for home field advantage for the first round of the playoffs. During the recent international window, Utah Royals FC captain, Kate Del Fava received her first USWNT senior team call up after receiving the news in person following the Royals’ 1-1 tie in Louisville. Del Fava’s first cap came in the second match between USA and Spain where she contributed to the Stars and Stripes second goal. Del Fava played an incredible ball over the top of the Spanish defense to teammate Michelle Cooper, who controlled it at the top of the penalty area. Cooper played the ball back to the penalty spot for an onrushing Malley Swanson, whose shot rippled the back of the net past the diving Spanish goalkeeper to tie the game at 2-2. Del Fava received her call up after being recognized as one of the top NWSL defenders this season as she was named to the NWSL Best XI for the months of May and July. The 28-year old defender has showcased her strong defensive abilities with the most clearances on the team with nearly double the next closest player with 135 in total and the most headed duels won with 53. Supporting the team on the offensive side, Del Fava scored both of her goals this season just a week apart. Her first goal came off a corner kick whipped to the far post, where Del Fava headed in the opening goal of the Royals’ 4-1 victory over North Carolina on July 25. Her second goal came in similar fashion, with another corner kick looped to the far post for Del Fava to head home the fifth goal in the Royals’ 5-1 home victory over the Portland Thorns. Del Fava has a long-standing history with Kansas City Current, having relocated with the team from Utah to Kansas City in 2021. During her time with the Current, she made 53 appearances, including 43 starts. Del Fava would return to Utah in 2024 through the expansion draft, where she has made an impressive club-record 79 consecutive starts and logged the most minutes in club history with 7,110. Since returning to the NWSL in 2024, the Royals have never taken a single point off the Current with a record of 0-5-0 (W-L-T) and getting outscored eight to one in the five contests. The last clash between the two ended in a 2-1 loss for the Royals despite heading into halftime with a 1-0 lead. Tatumn Milazzo scored the lone Royals goal off a short worked corner that Cloé Lacasse whipped into the six-yard box. Milazzo was able to get her head to the ball before the Current goalkeeper could punch it away for the first Royals goal of the 2026 season. This season, a bulk of Kansas City’s goals have come from the front four with 34 of the team’s 48 goals split between the forwards. Leading the attack is two-time Golden Boot winner Temwa Chawinga, who won her first Golden Boot when she set the NWSL single-season scoring record back in 2024 with 20 goals. During the 2025 season, Chawinga scored 15 goals and recorded three assists on her way to winning her second consecutive NWSL Golden Boot. Supporting Chawinga in the attack has been veteran forwards, Haley Hopkins, who scored a hattrick two games ago against Denver Summit, and Debinha, who scored a hattrick of her own in the Current’s last match against Bay FC. USWNT winger Michelle Cooper has recorded 10 goal involvements this season as the 2025 NWSL Shield winners look to secure its spot in the playoffs. The battle against Kansas City will take place at America First Field on October 17th with kickoff scheduled for 4:30 p.m. MT. Tickets are available at www.rsl.com/utahroyals/tickets/. title: Podcast Release: The Supreme Court Opinions in Trump v. Slaughter and Trump v. Cook: What Do They Mean for the Future of the Administrative State? - Consumer Finance Monitor
content: CFPB, Federal Agencies, State Agencies, and Attorneys General The Supreme Court’s June 29, 2026 decisions in Trump v. Slaughter and Trump v. Cook raise fundamental questions about presidential power, the independence of federal agencies, and the constitutional structure of the administrative state. Although both cases involved the President’s authority to remove federal officials, the Court’s decisions appear to point in different directions. In our latest Consumer Finance Monitor podcast, our host, Alan Kaplinsky (founder and former practice group leader for 25 years and now Senior Counsel of our Consumer Financial Financial Services Group) discuss these decisions and their potentially far-reaching implications with Professor Lev Menand of Columbia Law School, one of the country’s leading scholars on administrative law, constitutional structure, financial regulation, and the Federal Reserve System. In Trump v. Slaughter, the Court, in a 6–3 decision authored by Chief Justice John Roberts, held that the Federal Trade Commission Act’s restrictions on the President’s ability to remove FTC commissioners violate the separation of powers. The Court concluded that FTC commissioners exercise substantial executive authority and therefore must remain accountable to the President through his removal power. In reaching that conclusion, the Court expressly overruled its 1935 decision in Humphrey’s Executor v. United States, which had upheld restrictions on the President’s removal of FTC commissioners. The decision represents a major development in the Court’s embrace of the unitary executive theory and could have significant consequences for the structure and independence of federal agencies. Justice Sonia Sotomayor, joined by Justices Elena Kagan and Ketanji Brown Jackson, dissented, arguing that the majority had discarded nearly a century of precedent and fundamentally altered the structure of independent agencies. Justice Neil Gorsuch, while concurring in the judgment, raised an additional constitutional concern: whether Congress has delegated excessive legislative authority to administrative agencies. In Trump v. Cook, decided the same day, the Court took a different approach to the attempted removal of Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook. In a 5–4 decision, the Court left in place an injunction preventing her removal while litigation continues. Although the Court did not resolve the ultimate merits of the dispute, it suggested that the Federal Reserve may occupy a unique constitutional position, drawing on historical references to the First and Second Banks of the United States. In our discussion, Professor Menand questions the historical analogy between those early banks and the modern Federal Reserve Board, emphasizing the distinction between a bank (which is what the First and Second Banks of the United States were) and a government agency that regulates banks (which is a significant part of what the Federal Reserve Board does.) We explore whether Cook establishes a meaningful exception to Slaughter, how far that exception might extend, and whether other financial regulators, including the FDIC, might be able to invoke similar arguments to preserve their independence. Our conversation also examines several other important issues: Professor Menand views Slaughter as one of the most consequential separation-of-powers decisions in American history and questions whether the Court’s reasoning adequately accounts for the longstanding role of independent agencies in the federal regulatory system. He also cautions that the decisions may have consequences extending well beyond presidential removal authority, potentially affecting the ability of the federal government to establish consistent national regulatory standards. The discussion concludes with Professor Menand’s assessment of where the law may be headed over the next five years and why the long-term consequences of these decisions remain difficult to predict. Listen to our latest Consumer Finance Monitor podcast for an in-depth discussion of these consequential decisions and their implications for the future of the administrative state and federal financial regulation. Postscript: Trump Establishes Committee to Reconsider Lisa Cook’s Removal Since recording this podcast, President Trump has announced a new effort to remove Federal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook. On October 7, Trump established a three-member committee of inquiry to investigate allegations that Cook made false statements in connection with mortgage documents and to recommend whether there is “cause” for her removal under the Federal Reserve Act. The committee consists of Kevin Hassett, director of the National Economic Council; Keith Sonderling, acting director of the Office of Government Ethics; and Andrea Lucas, chair of the Equal Employment Opportunity Commission. The committee is scheduled to hold a closed, transcribed hearing at the White House on November 5, at which Cook may respond to the allegations and present evidence and arguments through counsel. It must provide written findings and a recommendation to Trump after receiving any post-hearing submission from Cook, due November 10. The initiative follows the Supreme Court’s June decision leaving in place an injunction against Cook’s removal while litigation proceeds, with the Court emphasizing the need to provide her notice of the allegations and an opportunity to respond. Cook’s attorneys have questioned whether the new process will be impartial, pointing to Trump’s repeated statements that he has already decided to fire her. The committee’s proceedings could therefore provide an important test of the procedural requirements governing a President’s authority to remove a Federal Reserve governor for cause. by the Consumer Financial Services Group at Ballard Spahr LLP

title: Paxton v Talarico: tens of millions of dollars pour into closely watched Texas Senate race - The Guardian
content: Elon Musk has spent $158m in a month to back Republicans in midterm races – with his efforts mostly focused on Texas Tens of millions of dollars are pouring into Texas as Democrats stage an audacious bid to win a US Senate seat in the Republican stronghold. Elon Musk, the world’s richest person, is among those wading into the closely watched race as November’s midterm elections approach. In September alone, Musk gave $158m to the Senate Leadership Fund, the primary super political action committee (Pac) backing Republican Senate candidates, Axios first reported. The donation accounted for more than half of the Senate Leadership Fund’s fundraising in the third quarter. Separately, Musk donated $10m to Lone Star Liberty Pac, the committee dedicated to supporting Ken Paxton, the Republican candidate in Texas, after Alex Latcham, the president of the Senate Leadership Fund, requested the funding. A source familiar with the matter confirmed Axios’s reporting to the Guardian. The Guardian has also asked representatives for America Pac, the political operation founded by Musk, for comment. The donations came as Republicans were struggling to keep up with spending by Paxton’s Democratic opponent, James Talarico. Over the summer, Talarico released an ad painting Paxton negatively as a politician with a history of corruption. Talarico, a young, progressive candidate known for his faith-based messaging, made strides with liberal voters in Texas when he defeated an established Democrat for the Senate nomination earlier this year. Talarico raised $64m – the largest third-quarter fundraising of a Senate candidate in history, just this summer, Politico reported. “He’s fighting this battle basically alone while Elon Musk and the full weight of the GOP fundraising apparatus outspends him 2:1. This is still an uphill battle,” an unnamed Democratic strategist working in Texas told Politico. Polls have shown the two candidates are essentially tied, though some have Talarico polling narrowly ahead of Paxton. The Texas Senate race is one of the most competitive races in the country and was expected to cost millions of dollars because it’s an expensive state to run a campaign. The Senate Leadership Fund warned, months earlier, that supporting Paxton would cost anywhere from $150m to $200m. But Donald Trump chose Paxton himself to run against Talarico. When Musk’s team and the Senate Leadership Fund analyzed polling, they found Paxton’s chances of winning dwindling, leading Musk to step in, Axios reported. Bernie Sanders, Robert Reich, Stacey Abrams, Medhi Hasan, Paul Krugman and other bold thinkers on how to defeat Trumpism and build a better future. From our opinion desk. In the 2025-2026 election cycle, Musk has donated approximately $366m to federal committees, the New York Times reported earlier this week. That is significantly more than he did during the 2024 election cycle, when he gave about $290m to help Trump. The increase in spending contradicts a statement Musk made in May 2025 when he predicted: “I think, in terms of political spending, I’m going to do a lot less in the future.” Andrew Romeo, a spokesperson for America Pac, told the New York Times: “These robust investments have allowed the GOP apparatus to get its message out so Republicans can have a fighting chance to defy history. “If Democrats take control of Washington and win key gubernatorial and attorney general races this November, then America risks becoming a socialist, woke and borderless country,” Romeo added.

title: BTS’ V Gets Dinner With His Bandmates, Practices Spanish & Shows Off Massive L.A. Crash Pad in ‘3 Days in LA’ Vlog - Billboard
content:
The 21-minute look inside the singer's life was filmed last month before the group's shows at SoFi Stadium. BTS‘ V gives ARMY an up-close-and-personal view of life inside the K-pop supergroup’s bubble in his new 3 Days in LA vlog. The 21-minute selfie-camera mini-documentary opens with the 30-year-old singer making sure he knows how to use the settings on his phone’s camera before he heads out to a family dinner with the rest of the group and their crew. After a back-and-forth about the relative merits of digital versus film cameras, more adjustment of his angles and some plate sharing at the gourmet restaurant, V heads back to the group’s massive rented L.A. mansion. Fans get a glimpse of the expansive outside seating area, complete with a giant fountain and classical columned railings, before he tucks into his Spanish language lessons under the L.A. moon. “I’ll try my best to be able to talk to you all,” he says in halting Spanish, in what seemed like a bit of practice before the group winds down the Latin American portion of their ARIRANG world tour with a pair of upcoming live viewings from their shows in Argentina and Brazil on, respectively, Oct. 25 and Oct. 30. “I feel happy that I can understand more and more,” he adds in Spanish as gentle piano jazz accompaniment tinkles in the background. He then plays a snippet of what he says is his favorite Latin song, “Sabor a Mí,” which has been recorded by everyone from Luis Miguel to EXO and Los Lobos. Next up is a house tour, from the cavernous, all-white living room to a glimpse of the ornate indoor pool, with V lamenting that the place is so huge he sometimes gets lost. The singer then wishes viewers good night (in Spanish, of course), before stripping off his shirt and going to bed. After a hearty breakfast and a stroll through the game room for early morning table tennis and billiards, it’s time to head to SoFi Stadium for soundcheck, where the rest of the group — RM, Suga, Jin, j-hope, Jimin and Jung Kook — do check-ins on camera before strolling onto the stage for their Sept. 5 gig at the L.A. venue. They are greeted by shouts of the lucky ARMY members on hand to witness the warm-up, as the men take their turns on the mic before heading to the green room to chill. V effortlessly sets up the camera to catch the group enjoying some pre-show sashimi, with jokes about how Jin caught the fish himself. After changing into his stage costume, V brushes his teeth and catches RM doing elaborate frog-pose stretches to limber up for the high-energy performance. Then it’s on to the obligatory group selfie just before walking out for the sold-out show. The journey ends back at the house, where the men wind down and try to get some quiet time and do self-care ahead of their Sept. 6 SoFi gig. The vlog ends with a surprise early birthday celebration for RM and a bit of shooting around on an indoor basketball court. BTS will take the stage on Friday (Oct. 16) for the second of three gigs at Estadio Nacional Julio Martínez Prádanos in Santiago, Chile, ahead of the first of three gigs in Argentina.
